entities.name: porter of the tomb-sweeping party with a staff
entities.what: Adult man, a porter or servant at the east (rear) end of the returning tomb-sweeping party: short jacket belted over trousers, a small cap; walking west with his legs apart, body seen almost from the front, his right arm swinging out to the east. A long thin pole or staff slants up behind his head over his shoulder (its top at about (31110, 314)); nothing hangs from it that the strokes show.
entities.src: 名画记: 杨柳杂花装簇轿顶 (pin 6)
entities.note: Feet at about (31112, 445) and (31150, 450); painted height 97 px at foot v 448 (the party's other walkers just west, t2's, are 87-90 px). His west foot is crossed by the load hanging from the pole of the porter just south-west of him (t2's, feet about (31080, 540)), whose pole ends at about (31124, 414) and whose bundle hangs at (31104-31127, 437-483): that bundle is the other porter's, not his. The restyle draws the staff as a stick with a knob at its top and dresses him in a red jacket; colours are the restyle's. He is the only member of the party with feet at u >= 31100; the party's group is t2's (merge joins him to it). Facing read from the stride and the party's direction of travel (west, toward the city); his face turns to the viewer. SECOND PASS (willows): foot and head confirmed at zoom 3.2: feet (31108-31118, 452) and (31146-31155, 452), head (31124-31139, 352-368). The staff runs from his shoulder up-left to (31110, 312). At zoom 8 its top is a small dark knob about 5 x 9 px at (31108-31113, 312-321), with no blade, tines or crossbar. It is a plain staff, or at most a tool seen edge-on. Build a plain staff (carried prop).

entities.name: far pollarded willow, leaning west (top of the silk)
entities.what: Far pollarded old willow at the top of the silk: one stout trunk leaning north-west from its foot to a knobbly clubbed head at about (31145, 155), from which a fan of long straight bare shoots rises and one long limb reaches far west along the silk's top edge. Early spring, bare or a faint haze. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).
entities.vis: part: crown cut by the silk's top edge
entities.note: Trunk outlines from (31140, 175)/(31170, 170) down to (31177, 250)/(31200, 243); the foot ends in a small dark tick at (31197-31203, 247-257). Painted height from foot to the silk's edge 230 px (more is cut off). The restyle draws it the same way (base about (31195, 262)). Its crown interlaces with S1.tree.willow_far_31245 to the east; the long west limb reaches about u 30950 at v 40 over t2's range. MERGE: t2's S1.tree.far_tree_30985 (blotches 30955-31015, v 23-43) lies at the end of this tree's west limb: one of them may be the other (second pass). FRAME AGENT (second pass west accepted): S1.tree.far_tree_30985 is a far shrub, not this willow's twig ends (its blotches are knotted dots like S1.tree.far_shrubs_30860's clumps; this tree's west shoots are fine lines that thin out at about u 31000-31020, v 40-60): both are kept.

entities.name: far pollarded willow, upright (top of the silk)
entities.what: Far pollarded old willow at the top of the silk, beside S1.tree.willow_far_31190: an upright trunk to a knobbly head at about (31240, 165) with a fan of long bare shoots rising to the silk's top edge. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).
entities.vis: part: crown cut by the silk's top edge
entities.note: Trunk lines at u 31233-31253 from the head down to v 287-293; the restyle's base is (31245, 293). A thin vertical line at u 31236-31240 runs on far below the foot (v 180-460): it is a crease or seam line in the silk, not part of the tree. Painted height to the silk's edge 267 px (cut). Crown extremes approximate (they interlace with the neighbours').

entities.name: small far sapling or stump
entities.what: A small slender far tree or sapling: a thin straight stem about 50 px tall with a short second stem or fork just east of it (u 31355-31360, v 360-390), standing on the far ground under the crowns of the far willows. Bare.
entities.note: Two parallel faint lines at u 31325-31335 from v 340 to 395, and a shorter stroke at 31355-31360; a branch of the willow crowns above crosses its top at v 330-345, so its own top is uncertain. The restyle draws a small forked tree here (base about (31325, 400)). Other reading: a post or the frame of something small; there is no head or body, so not a figure. Painted height about 60 px at foot v 396. SECOND PASS (willows): at zoom 1-5 the two strokes read as the two outlines of one short thick stem, with no fork or twig at either top. The west outline runs at u 31326-31334 from v 338 to 394, the east outline at u 31353-31360 from v 358 to 384, with pale silk between. A willow branch crosses at v 330-345 and hides the top. A third reading (c): a cut stump or a low pollard about 30 px wide and 55 px tall, base (31342, 395). The far bank line S1.grd.bank_31390 (v 400-413 here) runs along its foot, and structures_w also called it 'a stump or tree knee'. Conf stays low. If (c) is taken, base becomes (31342, 395), `top` is dropped and the form is a stump.

entities.name: far pollarded willow (west of a pair)
entities.what: Far pollarded old willow on the ground above the great willows, the western of a pair: a short thick trunk to a dark knobbly head at about (31420-31477, 290-360), from which long bare shoots fan up to the silk's top edge, making with its neighbour S1.tree.willow_far_31505 one broad canopy over u 31250-31820. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).
entities.vis: part: crown cut by the silk's top edge
entities.note: Trunk outlines at u 31421-31430 and 31456-31464, v 344-413; foot at v 410-416. A faint ground band runs at v 393-400 west of it. Painted trunk height (foot to head) about 90 px; crown to the silk's edge 384 px. Crown extremes approximate (interlaced). The restyle draws it as a thick knobbly trunk (base about (31440, 420)). A long drooping branch from the crowns here reaches down to about (31385, 680): read as part of the crown of S1.tree.willow_great_31620 (its whips fan up from below).

entities.name: far pollarded willow (east of a pair)
entities.what: Far pollarded old willow, the eastern and nearer of a pair with S1.tree.willow_far_31443: a heavier knobbly trunk to a clubbed head at about (31477-31537, 293-360), throwing fans of long bare shoots up and to the east as far as u 31820. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).
entities.vis: part: crown cut by the silk's top edge
entities.note: Trunk outlines at u 31480-31490 and 31520-31537 from v 360 down to v 463-473; a dark lump at (31510-31533, 459-473) at the foot. Its foot is about 60 px lower on the silk than its neighbour's, so it stands nearer the viewer. A faint ground band at v 423-430 east of it. The restyle draws a big knobbly trunk with its base about (31530, 500) and invents nothing else here. Crown extremes approximate.

entities.name: great willow leaning across the hut's fence (hollow bole)
entities.what: A great old willow at the east end of the thatched hut, leaning hard north-west: its huge low hollow bole (a broad mottled mass about 150 px wide with a dark round hollow in its east face) sits on the bank just south of the shed's fence, and its trunk runs up-left past the west end of that fence, in front of the hut's wattle fence and east gable, to a pollard head at about the hut's eave, from which bare whips fan up over the hut's thatched roof. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.
entities.vis: part: trunk crosses in front of the fences; head and crown mixed with the hut's roof and the willow whips over it
entities.note: Bole extents about u 31150-31310, v 1330-1480, the hollow at (31260-31270, 1365-1375), its top at (31270, 1335); its foot merges with the dark wash of a bank at v 1405-1480, so the base is est. The trunk: a dark diagonal from the bole at (31150, 1345) to (31100, 1300), then a pale band with a dark west edge at u 31010-31100, v 1190-1330 (structures_w independently reads 'the leaning trunk of a big willow' here, in front of the fence at u 31017-31087), up to the eave at about (31000-31060, 1120-1150); the head is lost in the roof's hatching (the restyle puts a knobbly head at (30850-30920, 1020-1100)), and the fans of whips over the roof (u 30950-31330, v 550-1000) are taken as its crown, so top and crown points are est. Readings: (a, kept) one great leaning willow rooted in the bole (the restyle draws exactly this); (b) the bole is a separate cut stump or a rock on the bank, and the trunk at u 31010-31100 belongs to a tree rooted at the fence's foot at about (31060, 1340) (t2's range), whose crown is the same whips. Under (b) the trunk's tree is t2's and the bole is a stump (mine) or a rock (structures_w's). The fence strokes above the bole (u 31120-31285, v 1100-1310) are drawn whole, so nothing rises in front of the fence's east part. Settle at the second pass on a zoom-3 read of u 31000-31320, v 1100-1490. MERGE: crown_w and top moved to t2's reading (crown_w (30290, 1050), top (30780, 560), both est; were (30900, 950) and (31100, 600)): on a zoom-0.7 crop of u 30200-31400 the pollard head is at about (30860-30990, 990-1120), the trunk runs unbroken from it down-right in front of the hut's fence into the hollow bole, and its whips fan west over the farmhouse to u ~30290 and up to v ~560. t1's "willow crown over the farmhouse's east end, trunk east of 30300" (u 30290-30460, v 800-1190) is this crown. Reading (a) looks right at this zoom: conf raised to med; the second pass confirms at zoom 3. SECOND PASS (west), the flagged zoom-3 read of u 31000-31320, v 1100-1490: reading (a) holds. On zoom 1.6 and 2.5 crops the trunk is one band: from the bole's upper west side (31150, 1345) diagonal strokes run up-left to the fence's foot at (31046-31102, 1297-1335); a pale band with a dark west edge rises at u 31008-31046 from v 1310 to the hut's eave (v ~1122); above the eave a dark trunk section at u 30902-30940 (v 1054-1190) carries it on up-left to the pollard head in the roof's hatching at about (30860-30990, 990-1120). No foot is drawn under the trunk at the fence (reading (b)'s 'tree rooted at the fence's foot at about (31060, 1340)'): the fence's withies run on, unbroken, behind it. The restyle draws the same single leaning willow. The bole's lower edge: I read it at v 1482-1498 across u 31150-31290, as the willows pass does; I agree with its base (31215, 1492, est) and its note on S1.road.main's edge_n. SECOND PASS (willows): the bole's lower edge is drawn at v 1486-1498 across u 31140-31275. Crops: zoom 2.4 greyscale and zoom 3 colour. The bole is the textured mass with bark marks, a pale crack at u 31176-31201 running down to v 1486, and the round hollow at (31255-31284, 1357-1382). Below the edge is a strip of pale ground (v 1498-1510), then the next dark wash (v 1510-1527). Row profiles: at v 1500 the silk turns pale (123-140) from u 31240 east, and at v 1480-1490 from u 31280 east; u 31140-31230 stays dark (100-113) down to v 1500-1505. The base moves from (31240, 1465) est to the middle of that edge. The mass is a tree's bole, not a rock: it has bark texture and a hollow, and diagonal strokes leave its upper west side (31120-31160, 1300-1340) toward the trunk in front of the fence. That fits reading (a). The trunk, head and crown west of u 31100 are the west pass's to settle.

entities.name: great willow leaning north-west (west of the four)
entities.what: One of the great old willows of 隋堤烟柳, the westernmost of four: a massive pale-barked trunk with dark knots and hollows (one big eye at about (31576, 1166)), leaning north-west from its foot to a broad knobbly pollard head at about (31430-31560, 940-1000), from which long straight bare whips fan up and far to the west over the shed on posts, to about u 31150 and v 400. A small fan of young shoots springs from its east side at about (31610, 1040). Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.
entities.note: Trunk west outline (31500, 1000) -> (31560, 1180) -> (31600, 1300); its lower trunk is the dark band at u 31600-31645 (brightness profile at v 1300-1325), ending on a pale ground band at v 1335-1345. Its foot touches the foot of S1.tree.willow_great_31715 (about 85 px apart, centre to centre): read as two trees whose feet meet, not one twin-trunked tree, since each trunk has its own outline down to the ground (the restyle reads them the same way). A pale rounded lump at its west foot (31545-31600, 1255-1345) is a root or a rock: left to structures_w. Painted height foot to crown top about 940 px; crown extremes approximate (the whips interlace with the far willows' and the neighbours'). MERGE: the pale rounded lump at its west foot (31545-31600, 1255-1345) is read on a zoom-2 crop as this tree's exposed root flare, joined to the trunk's outline: part of the tree, not a rock (no entity).

entities.name: great knobbly willow leaning north-east
entities.what: Great old willow of 隋堤烟柳, second from the west: a massive dark knobbly burled trunk rising from a foot shared with its western neighbour and leaning north-east, widening upward and dividing in its upper part into two knobbly stems (u about 31680-31700 and 31730-31800 at v 1000-1100), to a clubbed pollard head at about (31690-31800, 890-960) with a fan of long bare whips. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.
entities.note: Dark lower trunk at u 31660-31760 at v 1300-1325 (brightness profile), ending at v about 1335; the trunk is about 100 px wide at v 1000-1100. That the upper part is two stems (not two trees) is read from one outline at the foot: conf of the two-stem reading med. Its foot meets S1.tree.willow_great_31620's at about u 31650. Crown top and extremes approximate (interlaced).

entities.name: great willow leaning north-west, burled middle
entities.what: Great old willow of 隋堤烟柳, third from the west: a tall trunk leaning north-west from its foot, pale-barked above and with dark swollen burls in its middle (about v 1130-1300) where it presses against the burled willow to the east, rising to a knobbly pollard head at about (31800-31900, 930-1000) from which bare whips fan up into the shared canopy. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.
entities.note: Its outline: a pale upper trunk at u 31800-31900 (v 1030-1150) slanting down-right; a west outline at u 31875-31885 from v 1300 to 1390 (brightness profile); the foot's east side meets the burled willow S1.tree.willow_great_burl_32065 at about u 31990-32020. Base taken at (31910, 1385), between the readings: structures_w's bank note reads this trunk's foot as u 31835-31939 at v 1359 (centre 31887), the restyle as 31869-31953 at v 1400, and the profile's outline gives 31880-31940. Which strokes belong to it and which to its east neighbour in the burled middle (31860-31990, 1130-1300) is the hardest read here: conf med. A gap of open silk between its upper trunk and the burled willow at (31892-31975, 950-1140). Crown extremes approximate.

entities.name: greatest burled willow of 隋堤烟柳
entities.what: The largest of the great old willows: a huge dark burled bole, very knobbly, with big swollen burls on its east side (about (32040-32110, 1000-1080) and (32050-32120, 1210-1270)), rising slightly north-west to a clubbed pollard head at about (31930-32060, 840-940), from which a dome of fine bare twigs and whips rises to v 242; at its foot the roots spread like rocks east to u 32270 and west to 31960. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.
entities.note: Trunk at v 1380-1410 spans u 32020-32140 (brightness profile); root flare from (31960, 1470) to (32270, 1560) (dark rocky strokes: the roots, not separate rocks; the restyle draws them as roots too). Painted height foot to crown top about 1210 px, the tallest tree in S1 so far. Its crown meets that of the willow whose head is at about (32250-32300, 1000-1100) and whose trunk runs down-right past u 32300 (t4's tree).

entities.name: large jar with a tied cover, under the shed on posts
entities.what: A large earthenware storage jar standing on the ground under the shed on posts, its mouth covered with a cloth tied round the neck; a rounded shoulder bulging to the east. About 50 px wide and 65 px tall.
entities.note: Outline u 31272-31325, v 1102-1172; the tied cover at (31275-31302, 1102-1117). The tile brief's 'figure' under the shed: on the scan at zoom 3-4 this is a jar (no head, no limbs), and the restyle also draws a jar with a tied cloth; no figure is painted under the shed. A few unclear strokes between it and the basin (31312-31332, 1137-1165) are read as the jar's and the basin's own outlines, not a separate thing.

entities.name: shallow round basin or tub, under the shed on posts
entities.what: A wide shallow round basin or low tub with a rim, set on the ground (or on a low stand) under the shed on posts, east of the tied jar; empty as far as the strokes show. About 77 px across.
entities.note: Rim ellipse u 31335-31412, v 1136-1160 with an inner rim; a lower outline at about (31320-31400, 1152-1162) is its body or a low stand. The shed's west post (structures_w's) passes in front of it at u 31353-31363. Other reading: a round tray on a low table. The restyle draws a shallow round basin. SCALE CUE: 77 px across, 22 px from rim to foot at foot v 1155-1162.
